finding: Final RX handoff cleared every processed slot, including NI tail payloads not yet eligible for reuse; stop errors were not propagated to DMA allocation release.
changes: Validate NI consumption and ARM completion before returning outstanding RXBD slots.
Recycle held buffers only at the original two-descriptor release distance; replace a final NI-tail RXBD while preserving its original payload.
Advance the returned cursor as each slot is handed back and preserve tail records through subsequent resume.
Propagate RX/NI/PE stop results through TX release and PCI teardown; detach ARM work and interrupt callbacks when DMA release cannot complete.

handoff.scope: Actual current and baseline ARM stop/start functions with DMA/IRQ and empty exception-drain callbacks. No physical DMA timing or hardware teardown test.

release_boundary.scope: Current TX release function with controlled NI/PE completion and DMA/IRQ callbacks; not a hardware teardown test.

stock_research: analysis/private/ni-queue-release66-stock.asm: board ca_ni_cleanup_tx_dma_lso frees allocation arrays, not proof of per-VP pipeline drain. Vendor ca_ni_reset_tx_ring resets software cursors; global engine completion remains a separate requirement.
scope: Actual baseline/current ARM handoff and TX release with controlled DMA/IRQ callbacks. Native radio module with current PE compiled; no hardware command, load or flash.
remaining: Live verification of local VP disable/base-reload versus outstanding NI payload reads before successful module unload.
When hardware drain fails, owned allocations are retained; recovery/reclamation of that retained state has not been implemented or proved.
A/B 121 versus30 RP report register/cadence and maximum throughput; sustained high-rate upload/download and physical PCIe refill visibility.
